\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فرمان} (farmân)}{فرمان (farmân)}]{\fa{فرمان} (farmân) — a steering wheel; a command, an order}

\label{lesson:FA-C420-farman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an invoice, then the Persian for a cash machine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فرمان}}
\textbf{\fa{فرمان}} (\emph{farmân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a steering wheel; a command, an order\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{فرمان} \fa{ماشین} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{دو} \fa{دست} \fa{میگیرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedaram farmân-e mâshin râ bâ do dast migirad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father holds the steering wheel with both hands.
\end{quote}

The older sense is a command or a royal decree. \emph{Posht-e farmân} — at the wheel, driving.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{farmân} is inherited: EtymDB traces it through Middle Persian \emph{framān} to Old Persian \emph{framānā} 'command'. The wheel is the part of the car that gives the orders.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farmân}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رانندگی} \fa{کردن} (rânandegi kardan)}{رانندگی کردن (rânandegi kardan)}]{\fa{رانندگی} \fa{کردن} (rânandegi kardan) — to drive (a car)}

\label{lesson:FA-C420-ranandegi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a cash machine, then the Persian for a steering wheel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رانندگی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{رانندگی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{rânandegi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to drive (a car)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خواهرم} \fa{هر} \fa{روز} \fa{تا} \fa{دفتر} \fa{رانندگی} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khâharam har ruz tâ daftar rânandegi mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister drives to the office every day.
\end{quote}

\emph{rânandegi} — driving, from \emph{rânande} (a driver), + \emph{kardan}. Present stem \emph{kon-}: \emph{rânandegi mikonam} — I drive.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rânandegi kardan} is built from \emph{rânandegi} 'driving', formed on the native verb \emph{rândan} 'to drive', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', which is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a cash machine, then the Persian for a steering wheel, then say \emph{rânandegi kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دنده} (dande)}{دنده (dande)}]{\fa{دنده} (dande) — a gear (of a car); a rib}

\label{lesson:FA-C420-dande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a steering wheel, then the Persian for to drive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دنده}}
\textbf{\fa{دنده}} (\emph{dande}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gear (of a car); a rib\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{ماشین} \fa{پنج} \fa{دنده} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In mâshin panj dande dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This car has five gears.
\end{quote}

Also a rib of the body. \emph{Dande-ye 'aqab} — reverse gear.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dande} is a native Persian word for a rib, later also for the teeth and gears of a wheel. Its older history is not settled, and EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a steering wheel, then the Persian for to drive, then say \emph{dande} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دنده} \fa{عوض} \fa{کردن} (dande 'avaz kardan)}{دنده عوض کردن (dande 'avaz kardan)}]{\fa{دنده} \fa{عوض} \fa{کردن} (dande 'avaz kardan) — to change gear}

\label{lesson:FA-C420-dande-avaz-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to drive, then the Persian for a gear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دنده} \fa{عوض} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{دنده} \fa{عوض} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{dande 'avaz kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to change gear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{پیچ} \fa{دنده} \fa{عوض} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U qabl az pich dande 'avaz mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He changes gear before the bend.
\end{quote}

\emph{dande} 'gear' + \emph{'avaz} 'a change, an exchange' + \emph{kardan}. \emph{'Avaz kardan} on its own means to change or swap.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dande 'avaz kardan} is built from native \emph{dande} 'gear', \emph{'avaz} 'exchange', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{ʿiwaḍ} 'a substitute', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کلاچ} (kelâch)}{کلاچ (kelâch)}]{\fa{کلاچ} (kelâch) — a clutch (pedal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C420-kelach}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a gear, then the Persian for to change gear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کلاچ}}
\textbf{\fa{کلاچ}} (\emph{kelâch}) — \textquotedblleft{}a clutch (pedal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کلاچ} \fa{ماشین} \fa{برادرم} \fa{خیلی} \fa{سفت} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kelâch-e mâshin-e barâdaram kheyli seft ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The clutch in my brother's car is very stiff.
\end{quote}

\emph{Kelâch gereftan} — to press the clutch. Automatic cars have no \emph{kelâch}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kelâch} was borrowed from a European language and is usually traced to English \emph{clutch}, the pedal that grips and frees the engine. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
